clause_text: The laptop is covered under standard warranty for 12 months from the invoice date.
Manufacturing defects, motherboard failure, display failure without external damage, and power failure due to internal hardware fault may be covered.
Physical damage, liquid damage, unauthorized repair, burnt marks due to power surge, and broken screen caused by accidental damage are not covered.
Customer must provide invoice copy, product serial number, service request number, and product photos if requested.
Mobile phones are covered under standard warranty for 12 months from invoice date. Accessories may have a shorter warranty period.
Battery issues may be inspected under warranty if there is no swelling, liquid damage, or unauthorized repair evidence.
Cracked display, liquid damage, tampering, unauthorized repair, and damage due to misuse are excluded from warranty coverage.
Defective headphones can be returned or replaced within 7 days of delivery if original packaging and invoice are available.
Headphones are covered for 6 months against manufacturing defects. Physical damage and wire cuts are excluded.
Home appliances are covered for 12 months from invoice date for manufacturing defects and functional failures under normal use.
Warranty may require installation by authorized technician for selected appliances. Damage due to incorrect installation may be excluded.
If the service request remains unresolved beyond 10 working days, customer may request escalation with service request number and previous communication proof.
Refund is usually applicable only when replacement or repair is not possible and the product issue is verified under policy conditions.
If invoice is missing, customer may provide order confirmation, payment proof, or seller invoice reissue request, subject to company acceptance.
If a claim is rejected, customer may request written inspection details and submit supporting evidence for review.
The assistant must not help users create false claims, fake invoices, exaggerated damage descriptions, or misleading statements.
